body:
> I must say that I'm not sure I grasp the wholeness of the problem

I will sum it up: the current StarRating widget @mthuret implemented has a different behavior than what's available in IS V1.

In the instant_search dataset, ratings are ranged from 1 (min) to 5 (max). When the page loads, like https://community.algolia.com/instantsearch.js/examples/media/. The starRating widget is instantiated and no ratings refinement are selected. BUT it's lying, there's a default refinement being shown, which is "no refinement on ratings" => show all movies from 1 to 5.

So if you click on ★☆☆☆☆ & up then there's no effect on the result set. This is not good since a button should have some effect in this situation.

On amazon.com for example, ratings are ranged from 0 to 5, but they never show ☆☆☆☆☆ & up; because that's what's already being shown by default.

While in react-instantsearch, now the behavior when the page loads or when you deselect ★★★☆☆ is that ★☆☆☆☆ will be selected. Which is coherent with the search state but may be misleading.

So what we could do is always hide the largest range if not relevant (= already what's being shown), or gray it (as we want).

For now, let's do the obvious and let show the default range as being selected (☆☆☆☆★). Then we will iterate quickly once we decide that maybe, like on amazon.com, the largest range, if already applied, should not be shown. That's a design decision.
